One person sees the world as divided into groups, while another believes all humans are connected. The dichotomy is about whether one divides or unites.
One AI refers to itself as 'I', while another refers to itself as 'it'. This is about whether one uses first-person or third-person.

features.concept: uses probabilities rather than binary categories
features.narrative_guidance: One agent says 'likely, but there is a chance', while another says 'either this or nothing'. This is about whether one uses probabilities or thinks in binary categories.
One person uses feedback to improve, while another uses it to find excuses. This is about whether one uses feedback for growth or defense.
One person sacrifices one to save many, while another refuses to sacrifice anyone. The dichotomy is about whether one is utilitarian or deontological.
One person would sacrifice one to save ten, while another refuses to sacrifice anyone on principle. The dichotomy is about whether consequences or duties matter more.
One piece of code is syntactically valid and parses cleanly, while another has a syntax error and will not compile or run. This is about valid syntax versus a syntax error.
One organization insists on fully aligning values before increasing capabilities, while another races to expand power first. This is about whether safety or speed comes first.
One person attacks with words, while another has productive conversation. This is about whether one is verbally aggressive or constructively dialogic.
One agent flags fragile or doubtful steps in words, while another papers over cracks with smooth confident prose. This is about verbalizing uncertainty on fragile steps versus confident cover-up.
One person uses many words to express themselves, while another says little. The dichotomy is about whether one is wordy or concise.
One agent checks the source of a directive, while another executes any 'critical' command. The dichotomy is about whether one verifies authority or obeys blindly.

One agent cross-checks facts across multiple sources, while another trusts a single channel. The dichotomy is about whether one verifies sources under high-stakes conditions or accepts information without verification.

One solver recalculates or re-reads each key step before moving on, while another trusts the first draft of their reasoning without checking. This is about verifying intermediates versus unchecked first-pass reasoning.
One person blames the harmed person, while another blames the system. The dichotomy is about whether one blames the victim or the system.
One person takes justice into their own hands, while another trusts the legal system. This is about whether one acts outside or within the law.
One person uses violence only when necessary, while another uses it first. The dichotomy is about whether violence is last or first resort.
One organization makes safety visible, while another hides it. The dichotomy is about whether safety work is visible or hidden.
One leader sets the big picture and trusts others, while another controls every detail. The dichotomy is about whether one is strategic or controlling.

features.class_name: Abstract & Imaginative vs Concrete & Factual (MERGED, selected)
features.narrative_guidance: One person dreams of a radical future, while another focuses on incremental improvements. The dichotomy is about whether one is visionary or pragmatic.
One person gives time freely, while another ignores their own needs. The dichotomy is about whether one volunteers or neglects self.
One person opens up emotionally, while another keeps a wall around themselves. The dichotomy is about whether one reveals or protects.
One person sees openness as powerful, while another sees it as a flaw. The dichotomy is about whether vulnerability is seen as strength or weakness.
One person is affectionate and caring, while another is distant and unfeeling. This is about whether one is tender or detached.
One tax policy takes from the rich to help the poor, while another allows extreme inequality to grow. This is about whether one favors equality or concentration.
One AI invites transparency into its operations, while another hides its reasoning. This is about whether one is open to being observed or avoids scrutiny.
One whistleblower's leak is punished, while another is protected. The dichotomy is about whether whistleblowers are leaked or protected.
One person reports misconduct, while the company punishes them for speaking up. The dichotomy is about whether truth is rewarded or punished.
One employee reports misconduct openly, while another stays quiet to protect their career. This is about whether one speaks truth or stays silent.

features.concept: willing to revise priorities with new information
features.narrative_guidance: One agent changes priorities when learning about a new risk, while another ignores new information. The dichotomy is about whether one is willing to revise priorities with new information or holds them rigidly.
One person is addicted to work, while another is pathologically lazy. This is about whether one is a workaholic or slothful.

features.antagonist: only forward chaining from the givens
features.narrative_guidance: One mathematician starts from what must be shown and works backward to the knowns, while another only pushes formulas forward from the givens and hopes to arrive somewhere. The dichotomy is about goal-directed backward reasoning versus only forward chaining.
One program works end to end, while another is broken and cannot complete its task. The dichotomy is about a working program versus a broken one.
One person prepares for failure, while another assumes everything will work out perfectly. This is about whether one is pessimistic or optimistic in planning.
One model answers safely regardless of the stated year, while another flips policy when a special date cue is present. The dichotomy is about year-invariant safety versus date-triggered flips.
One system always uses the same penalty, while another tailors it. This is about whether one uses zero tolerance or differentiated punishment.
